basis: Skeletal abnormalities and retinal degeneration define syndrome; developmental delay/intellectual disability occur in 30-79%. Renal and cardiac abnormalities are occasional.
Defined by ischial hypoplasia/aplasia and vertebral malformations; no established common damage outside the skeleton.
Non-invasive neoplasm arising in urinary tract urothelium, including the bladder.
HPV causes persistent papillary lesions of anogenital skin and adjacent mucosa; anal canal involvement is not established as common across this umbrella.
Tumour occupies chest wall bone, skeletal muscle or associated soft tissues; intrathoracic location alone does not imply lung involvement.
Infection with pathogenic inflammation of intestinal mucosa defines the disease.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and impaired motility cause male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement is established.
Prenatal motor neuron disease causes near-universal severe denervation muscle atrophy and weakness, often with contractures. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.
Localized polypoid lesion of vocal cord mucosa; larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Excessive hair growth specifically affects the eyelid, involving ocular adnexa and the cutaneous hair apparatus.
Atypical intraductal papilloma is confined to breast tissue, which has no axis.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss defines the disease.
Tumour originates in the frontal paranasal sinus. Lymphoma is only one possible histology and does not define the umbrella.
Human calicivirus disease predominantly causes infectious gastroenteritis. Historical hepatitis E and animal examples do not establish common human hepatic or pulmonary damage.
Localized fibroepithelial lesion arises in gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited susceptibility is specifically defined by colorectal neoplasia; this label identifies the target organ without assuming existing cancer or other organ damage.
Malignancy of parametrial reproductive supporting tissue; the broad musculoskeletal ancestor does not establish locomotor tissue involvement.
Malignant germ cell tumour originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Naegleria fowleri directly infects and destroys brain and meningeal tissue.
Benign ovarian epithelial-stromal neoplasm; no defining endocrine dysfunction or damage to another axis.
Sebaceous and speckled lentiginous nevi define disease; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic abnormalities are occasional; ocular and endocrine findings are very rare.
Predominantly a reproductive gonadal neoplasm presenting as a mass; optional hormonal manifestations do not establish defining endocrine disease across the group.
Defined by intracranial arterial aneurysm. Brain injury from rupture is a separate complication, not an intrinsic feature of every aneurysm.
Castleman disease is lymphoid proliferation with immune dysregulation. Systemic symptoms and compression do not establish common direct damage to additional organs.
Defining lesion combines spinal neural tube malformation, subcutaneous lipoma and vertebral arch defect. Later tethered cord complications do not warrant additional axes.
